props.title: The Blonde One

sections.content: **The Blonde One** (2019) marks a significant evolution in Latin American LGBTQ+ cinema, following in the footsteps of **Y Tu Mamá También** (2001) and **Moonlight** (2016). Director Marco Berger crafts an intimate portrait of sexual awakening and masculine vulnerability in contemporary Argentina. The film's power lies in its patient observation of two roommates - Juan and Gabriel - as their relationship slowly transforms from awkward cohabitation to something deeper. Berger's signature long takes and focus on subtle gestures recalls the tender masculinity studies of **Weekend** (2011) and **Call Me By Your Name** (2017).

sections.content: Berger's filmmaking approach in **The Blonde One** builds on his earlier work like **Plan B** (2009) and **Hawaii** (2013), establishing him as a master of depicting unspoken desire through charged silences and meaningful glances. The film's exploration of class differences and urban isolation connects it to other contemporary queer cinema like **God's Own Country** (2017) and **BPM (Beats Per Minute)** (2017), though Berger's style remains distinctly minimalist and observational.

The film's portrayal of working-class masculinity and repressed desire echoes themes found in **Eastern Boys** (2013) and **Stranger by the Lake** (2013), but with a distinctly South American perspective on machismo culture. Berger's careful attention to domestic spaces and routines recalls the intimate realism of **Keep the Lights On** (2012) while maintaining its own unique rhythm and visual language. sections.content: **The Blonde One** represents a crucial entry in the emerging wave of Latin American LGBTQ+ cinema, alongside works like **Mosquita y Mari** (2012) and **José** (2018). These films share a commitment to authentic representation while moving beyond traditional coming-out narratives. The naturalistic performances and unforced pacing allow for a deeper examination of how sexuality intersects with class, family, and cultural expectations in modern Latin America.
